examples.text: Die neuen Lampen verbreiten ein unangenehmes, grelles Licht.
examples.translation: Te nowe lampy dają nieprzyjemne, jaskrawe światło.

examples.text: Sie hat eine sehr hohe, grelle Stimme.

glosses: Éblouissant, voire aveuglant (en parlant d’une lumière).

examples.text: Der grelle Blitz des Fotoapparats ist mir unangenehm.

glosses: Strident, très aigu et fort (en parlant d’un son).

examples.text: Aus Versehen hat jemand die Alarmanlage ausgelöst und jetzt ertönt ein greller, unerträglicher Ton.
examples.translation: Quelqu’un a déclenché le système d’alarme par mégarde et maintenant, un son aigu et insupportable retentit.

glosses: Vif, acidulé, criard (en parlant d’une couleur).

examples.text: Ebenfalls angelockt werden (Wespen) durch bunte Farben, etwa grelle Kleidung – kein Wunder, ähneln diese doch den Blüten vieler Pflanzen. Parfüms und Cremes können sie ebenfalls anlocken.
examples.translation: Les (guêpes) sont également attirées par les couleurs vives, par exemple les vêtements criards - ce qui n'est pas étonnant, puisqu'ils ressemblent aux fleurs de nombreuses plantes. Les parfums et les crèmes peuvent également les attirer.

examples.text: Ich wurde vom grellen Licht der Scheinwerfer geblendet.

glosses: Pruriently detailed and sensationalistic about something shocking or horrifying, especially with regard to violence or sex.

examples.text: The accident was described with lurid detail.
Speculating on why publishers rejected it, he wonders whether it was deemed too lurid at the time, especially since Steinbeck was then an unknown author.
Fierce o'er their beauty blazed the lurid flame;
Wrapt in drifts of lurid smoke / On the misty river-tide.
The great banths sniffed the unfamiliar odours, and then with a rush they broke past us with low growls, swarming across the gardens beneath the lurid light of the nearer moon.

glosses: Being of a light yellow hue.

examples.text: The lurid lighting of the bar made for a very hazy atmosphere.

glosses: Having a brown colour tinged with red.

examples.text: a lurid plant with maroon leaves and pink flowers

glosses: Showy; visually impressive, attention-getting, or appealing.

examples.text: The dancers wore flashy costumes featuring shiny sequins in many vibrant colors.

glosses: Marked by frequent variations in water amount (compare flash flood).

examples.text: Flow criteria were used for classification […] The criteria chosen were […] (4) the rate of change of flow with time (logged serial correlation coefficients are 0.2 in flashy rivers, but up to 0.98 in stable ones); and (5) the velocity associated with average daily flows (this varies from 1.03 m/s in flashy rivers to 0.08 m/s in lowland ones).
a flashy light

[…] the accustomed warmth pierced his marrow, and ran thrilling through his shaken bones; just as when at times, with forked thunder burst, a chinky stream of fire in flashy lightning shoots athwart the skies.

Indeed, he was 'dithguthted' at his condition; and if upon the occasion just described he had allowed himself to be somewhat 'intoxicated with liquor,' I must aver that I do not recollect another instance in which this worthy little gentleman suffered himself to be similarly overtaken. Now and then a little 'flashy' he might be, but nothing more serious—and rely upon it, this was no common virtue in those days.
